links.outcome: Deployed sensitivity/specificity versus FDA 510(k) cleared benchmark
links.effect: Sensitivity 64.1% (95% CI 61.5-66.6%), specificity 98.8% vs 93% sensitivity and 93.7% specificity in FDA 510(k) summary
links.quote: Overall sensitivity was 64.1% (95% CI, 61.5-66.6%), specificity 98.8% (95% CI, 98.6-99.0%), compared with 93% sensitivity and 93.7% specificity in the FDA 510(k) summary.

links.outcome: Sensitivity by clinical site and CT scanner
links.effect: Sensitivity 68.7% vs 55.7% (P < .001) at two highest-volume sites; CT scanner the only differing variable
links.quote: Sensitivity differed significantly between the two highest-volume sites, 68.7% and 55.7% (P < .001), with CT scanner as the only variable different between the two sites.

links.outcome: Temporal change in false-positive rate and sensitivity
links.effect: False-positive rate fell 40% per year (P<.001); sensitivity fell 15% per year at site A (P<.036), 72.5% to 65.0%
links.quote: The false-positive rate fell 40% per year (P<.001) at a similar rate at two sites, while sensitivity fell 15% per year at site A (P<.036), from 72.5% to 65.0% between two halves of the study period.

links.outcome: Sensitivity across embolus location and chronicity subgroups
links.effect: Sensitivity central 88.6%, lobar/segmental 63.1%, subsegmental 33.3%; acute 65.5%, chronic 57.4%
links.quote: Sensitivity fell with peripherality (central 88.6%, lobar or segmental 63.1%, subsegmental 33.3%) and with chronicity (acute 65.5%, chronic 57.4%).
